title: How to Automate KYB Verification Across Business Registries
summary: Learn how to automate KYB verification with Skyvern: search business registries, download filings, return results to your review sheet, and schedule checks.
body_markdown:
KYB, or Know Your Business, is the process of checking who you’re doing business with. Before you onboard a business customer, supplier, or partner, you confirm its registration details, understand who owns or controls it, and check for risks such as sanctions exposure.


These checks take time: search a registry, find the right entity, download its filings, and copy the details into your review sheet. Open the next portal and do it again. Every new business adds another round of searches, downloads, and data entry.


This is exactly the kind of workflow we built Skyvern for. Skyvern can navigate the portals you configure, collect records, and return the information your team needs to review.


In this article, we’ll show you how to build that workflow: prepare your business list, automate registry searches, collect the results, and send exceptions to an analyst. We’ll also cover how to test the results and schedule repeat checks.


## Choose a simple KYB check to automate


We recommend to start with a check your team repeats often and can describe precisely.


Fro example, a registry lookup: take a business’s legal name and registration number, open its record, collect the required fields, and save any supporting filings.


Choose one registry where automated access is permitted and a small set of businesses your team has already reviewed. Those cases give you something to compare the automation against. Once the lookup works, you can extend it to more businesses and sources.


Before building, you'll need four things:


- **Inputs:** the case ID, legal name, registration number, jurisdiction, and registry URL.
- **Matching rules:** how to identify the correct entity and what to do when several records could match.
- **Required results:** the fields and documents your analyst needs from this particular source.
- **Exceptions:** missing records, ambiguous matches, unavailable documents, and searches that fail.


Use the registry lookup as one step in your existing KYB process. Your team’s ownership checks, screening requirements, and approval rules determine what happens after the result comes back.


Keep each search result and supporting file tied to the same case ID.


## Build the KYB workflow in Skyvern


In Skyvern, a saved, reusable workflow is called an **agent** . You describe the job to Copilot, review the steps it builds in Studio, and run the agent with your business details. We’ll use the registry lookup above as the example.


### 1. Prepare your business list


Create one row per business with the inputs you defined. Keep the case ID consistent across the input sheet, returned records, and downloaded documents so your team can trace each result back to the application.


Check the list before running it. A trading name entered as the legal name, a missing jurisdiction, or a registration number stripped of its leading zeros can send the search toward the wrong record. Store registration numbers as text where necessary.


If you use Google Sheets, open **Integrations** in Skyvern and connect the account that has access to your sheet. The connection supports[Google Sheets Read and Google Sheets Write blocks](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/integrations) . Keep the submitted information in its own columns; write the registry’s values into separate columns so discrepancies stay visible.


### 2. Describe the registry check to Copilot


On Skyvern’s **Home** page, describe the site, the task, and the result you want. Include the actual registry URL and explain which values will change between runs. For example:


> Build a reusable agent for our business registry checks. Take the case ID, legal name, registration number, jurisdiction, and approved registry URL as inputs. Search by registration number when available; otherwise use the legal name and jurisdiction. Open the matching entity record and return its legal name, registration number, status, formation date, registered agent, and record URL. Download the required filings when available. If several records could match, return them for review. Mark fields the registry does not publish as unavailable. Record a failed search separately from a completed search with no matching entity. Keep every result tied to the case ID.


Adapt the requested fields and filings to the source. A registry that publishes registered-agent details may not publish beneficial ownership information, and an agent should not fill that gap by treating the registered agent as an owner.


### 3. Review the steps in Studio


Skyvern opens the agent in **Studio** , where Copilot builds blocks and tests them in a browser. Review the proposed changes and their test status before accepting them. Once accepted, the changes are saved to the agent. The[first-agent guide](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/quickstart) shows this flow.


Check that the proposed steps cover the whole lookup: opening the correct portal, entering the search, selecting the entity, collecting its details, and retrieving the requested documents. If the portal requires a login, connect a saved credential for later runs.


A **Browser Task** block can handle navigation and search. An **Extraction** block collects structured fields from the page, and a **File Download** block can retrieve documents. Copilot can assemble these steps; the[block reference](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/reference/blocks) explains their settings if you need to adjust them yourself.


An illustrative block sequence for collecting a registry record and its supporting filings.


### 4. Define the result your analyst will receive


Decide how the output should look before adding more sources. Consistent fields let your review sheet show what was searched, what the registry returned, and what needs attention.


The following is a suggested output structure to configure for this workflow:


Field What to return


Case ID The identifier supplied with the application


Check outcome Matched, ambiguous, no record found, or search failed


Registry values Legal name, registration number, status, and other requested fields the source publishes


Source record Registry name, record URL, and check time


Supporting documents References to the filings or other files collected


Review reason The mismatch, missing information, or search problem that needs attention


Keep the **check outcome** separate from the **registry status** . “Matched” means the workflow found an entity using your matching rules. The registry might still describe that entity as inactive. Neither value records your team’s final onboarding decision.


Skyvern’s run **Outputs** view contains extracted information and downloaded files. The Browser pane provides screenshots of the steps. Use those[run records](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs) to inspect the result and retain the documents your process requires. Save required files to your case storage; temporary download links should not be your only record.


### 5. Repeat the check for each business


After the first lookup works, ask Copilot to read your input list and repeat the check for each row. Use a **Loop** block to pass each business’s details into the search and collection steps.


Configure how the loop handles failures. You may want one failed search to return an exception while the agent continues with the next business. Confirm that the failed case still appears in the output with its case ID and reason. A missing result should never silently disappear from the batch.


Compare the number of input businesses with the number of recorded outcomes. Each attempted check should have a result, including those that need another attempt or an analyst’s attention.


### 6. Return results to the review sheet


Add a **Google Sheets Write** block to write the returned fields into your results sheet, or pass them into the process your team already uses. Include the case ID and source so results from different portals can be grouped correctly.


Use conditional branches to separate straightforward matches from exceptions. For an ambiguous match, retain the candidate records and explain why the workflow could not choose one. For a missing field, distinguish information the registry does not publish from information the agent failed to retrieve.


Assign an owner to the exception queue. The workflow has completed its job when the analyst receives usable results and a clear reason for any review.


Example data: record every outcome, including ambiguous matches and failed searches.


## Connect the other sources your process requires


Once the first registry check works, add the next source your team uses. Give each source its own search instructions, matching rules, and expected fields. A company registry, a licensing board, and a sanctions source each answer a different question.


Use this table to plan what the next check should collect:


Source What it provides What to keep with the case


[California bizfile](https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/business-entities/information-requests?ref=skyvern.com) Entity name and number, status, formation or registration date, addresses, agent, and available officer or manager information Entity record, relevant filings, source URL, and check time


[Virginia SCC’s Clerk’s Information System](https://www.scc.virginia.gov/businesses/business-faqs/reinstatements/?ref=skyvern.com) Business entity search and current status; further details and documents depend on the record Entity ID, status record, and supporting filings or certificates obtained


[Delaware Division of Corporations](https://corp.delaware.gov/faqs/?ref=skyvern.com) Free entity details including file number, formation date, and registered agent; status is a separate paid service Entity details and any separately obtained status result or certificate


[OFAC sanctions sources](https://ofac.treasury.gov/sanctions-list-service?ref=skyvern.com) SDN and other OFAC list records for screening Search inputs, potential matches, identifying details, and the analyst’s resolution


[SAM.gov exclusions](https://www.acquisition.gov/far/9.404?ref=skyvern.com) Federal exclusion records, including the issuing authority, cause, effect, and termination date Relevant exclusion record and its effect on the proposed relationship


Licensing boards and regulators, such as[Virginia’s insurance regulator](https://www.scc.virginia.gov/boi/consumerinquiry/search.aspx?ref=skyvern.com) License information for the relevant business or professional License number, type, available status details, and source record


Check access conditions before adding a portal. Delaware’s[entity search](https://icis.corp.delaware.gov/ecorp/EntitySearch/NameSearch.aspx?ref=skyvern.com) restricts data mining and warns that automated tools may result in suspended access. Use a permitted service or another approved retrieval method for that source. The free search also returns active and inactive entities without establishing current status; even its separate[online status result](https://corp.delaware.gov/onlinestatus/?ref=skyvern.com) is not an official certificate of good standing.


For sanctions searches, return potential matches with enough identifying information for investigation.[OFAC’s guidance on assessing a match](https://ofac.treasury.gov/faqs/5?ref=skyvern.com) explains why the name alone is insufficient. Keep screening outcomes distinct from registry and licensing results.


### Use your existing KYB API where it covers the check


If a data provider already returns the information and documents you need, build around that coverage. Compare the actual fields, jurisdictions, source freshness, and document access before adding another lookup.


Skyvern can handle permitted portal work that remains, such as collecting a particular filing or checking a specialist licensing site. Keep the provider’s results and the browser-retrieved records under the same case ID. This makes[public records retrieval](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/automate-public-records-retrieval/) part of the existing review process.


## Test the workflow before increasing volume


Use cases your analysts have already checked and compare the automation with their results. Include more than clean matches: the exception handling needs testing too.


Test case What to verify


Known entity with a registration number The agent opens the correct record and returns the source’s values


Several businesses with similar names The workflow uses the matching rules or returns the candidates for review


Field the source does not publish The result marks it unavailable without inventing a value


Search that completes with no match The result records that outcome with the search inputs


Failed search or document download The failure remains visible and the case is routed for follow-up


Open the downloaded documents and check that they belong to the selected business. Confirm that each output row has the correct case ID, source, and check time. If a result looks wrong, inspect the run’s Timeline, screenshots, and Outputs to find the step that needs adjusting.


Review the exception queue with the people who will use it. They should be able to identify the problem, open the supporting record, and record a decision without repeating the entire search. Analysts still investigate findings, resolve discrepancies, and make the final decision under your approval policy.


Expand the workload once the test cases produce the expected records and exceptions. Repeat the relevant tests when you add a source or change the matching rules.


## Schedule repeat checks and maintain the workflow


When the workflow is ready, open **Schedule** in Studio, add a schedule, and set its inputs, frequency, and timezone. Check the next scheduled runs before creating it. Skyvern’s[scheduling controls](https://www.skyvern.com/docs/cloud/runs) support recurring runs of saved agents.


Set the cadence for your process, then compare each new result with the prior record.


Choose the cadence around your existing monitoring requirements. Keep successive results with their check times and configure your review process to compare the fields that matter, such as registry status or license status. A scheduled run collects a new result; your comparison rules determine which changes need attention.


Review failed runs and exceptions regularly. If a portal changes its search or document flow, inspect the affected step, update the agent, and rerun the relevant test cases. Assign someone responsibility for maintaining each source’s workflow.


Measure completed checks, analyst review time, unresolved exceptions, and cost per check. Include data-provider charges, portal fees, automation costs, and review time. Track the time to a completed KYB decision separately from the time spent on an individual registry lookup.


## FAQ


### Can KYC or KYB verification checks across government and registry websites be automated?


Yes. Where access is permitted, browser automation can search records, retrieve available documents, and return information for review. Configure each source’s matching rules and expected results, and route ambiguous matches or failed checks to an analyst.


### How do I automate KYB checks for business customers without a large compliance team?


Start with one repetitive check and a small set of previously reviewed cases. Standardize the inputs, build the search and collection steps in Skyvern, and write the results into your review sheet. Use your existing KYB data provider where its coverage fits. Assign responsibility for exceptions before adding more businesses or sources.


### What is a red flag during KYB?


Examples include documents that conflict with official records, unexplained ownership changes, reluctance to provide required ownership information, or screening results that may concern the business or its owners. Configure the workflow to return the discrepancy and its source for investigation. An address difference may have a straightforward explanation, while a potential sanctions match needs assessment under the relevant procedures.


[Build your first KYB workflow in Skyvern](https://app.skyvern.com/?ref=skyvern.com) . Start with one approved registry, a small business list, and the results your analyst needs to review.
